_comment: Edit this file to change behaviour without a code change; it is re-read when it changes.
TARGET WEIGHTS (0..1): the ```json block of docs/research/russia_hybrid_targeting.md is the authority
and overrides 'weights' below when present; these are the same values, kept as the fallback.
Finding of the brief: the targets so far were military air bases, nuclear-sharing and naval bases, aid
logistics and civil airports - not stadiums. Stadiums/venues stay in the list at a low weight, raised
Shahed-136 / Geran-2 class fixed-wing one-way attack drone. PUBLIC OPEN-SOURCE ESTIMATES ONLY
(press reporting, think-tank and government briefings, e.g. CSIS, RUSI, ISW, Ukrainian Air Force):
maximum range roughly 1,500-2,500 km; cruise roughly 150-185 km/h; flies low, often 100-500 m,
on the approach. These are planning figures for 'what is in reach', not performance data.

targets._comment: Coastal target set: everything within coastal_band_km of the sea, top N per country per type.

alert._comment: Severity: critical when ALL of: link strength >= strong_link, loitering >= long_loiter_hours, and at least many_targets targets of weight >= high_weight (0.65 = civil airports and above in the brief) within in_range_km. Otherwise high.

_comment: Time multipliers from the research brief (section 5). They raise the TARGETS component of the score
(and the rank of the targets they touch); they never change whether an alert is raised.
night: local solar time from longitude. wave_days/wave_factor: after an entry in 'incidents'.
lat, lon, radius_km, start, end (ISO dates), factor (optional), types (optional list of target types)}.
A mass_event raises stadium_venue to mass_event_weight inside its radius; an election raises government x election_factor.

precursors._comment: Precursor indicators from the brief (section 6) scored as one component: each adds its points (0..1 in total).
